title: Separating one primary curve component from the remaining scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field] and let $X\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be a connected closed subscheme of dimension one [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with homogeneous-coordinate Hilbert polynomial $dm+c$, $d>0$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial]. Let $Y$ be a reduced irreducible component of dimension one [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-reduced-scheme], let $\xi$ be its generic point, and put $\mu=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi}}\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Put $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ and $e=\deg(\nu^*L|_Y)$ on the normalization $\nu:\widetilde Y\to Y$ [def-sc-normalization, def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Let $\mathcal I_Y=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], with powers as in [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Then $\mu$ is a finite positive integer. There exist a closed subscheme $C\subset X$, possibly empty, an integer $Q\ge1$, and an integer $c_C$ such that its Hilbert polynomial is
$$P_C(m)=(d-\mu e)m+c_C,\qquad \delta:=d-\mu e\ge0,$$
and restriction gives an injection
$$\mathcal I_Y^Q\longrightarrow\mathcal O_C.$$
Consequently, for all $t\ge Q$ and $m\ge0$, the restriction map $H^0(X,\mathcal I_Y^t\otimes L^{\otimes m})\longrightarrow H^0(C,L^{\otimes m}|_C)$ is injective. The one-dimensional irreducible components of $C$ are precisely the irreducible components of $X$ other than $Y$, with their ambient generic multiplicities preserved. If $Y$ is a proper subset of $|X|$, there is a closed point $P\in Y\cap C$ lying on a one-dimensional component of $C$. No generic reducedness is assumed, and embedded components of $X$ are allowed.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal] to write $X=\operatorname{Proj}(B/I)$, $B=k[x_0,\ldots,x_{r-1}]$. Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-primary-decomposition]. Let $\mathfrak p_1$ be the homogeneous prime of $Y$ and label its primary factor $Q_1$; it is minimal over $I$. Indeed in the affine charts of [def-pc-proj], components are minimal primes by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]; a smaller homogeneous prime remains relevant and would give a strictly larger component. Put $J=\bigcap_{a\ne1}Q_a$, with $J=B$ for a single factor, and $C=\operatorname{Proj}(B/J)$. All these ideals are finitely generated, since the decomposition node also states that $B$ is Noetherian. The quotient presentation [lem-sfb-polynomial-quotient-proj-presentation] supplies its projective closed embedding and properness. Since $I\subseteq J$, its chart quotient maps factor those of $X$, so $C\subseteq X$. The same presentation gives properness of $X$ and its reduced closed components.

proof.text: Choose $Q\ge1$ with $\mathfrak p_1^Q\subseteq Q_1$ by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-primary-decomposition]. Then $\mathfrak p_1^Q\cap J\subseteq Q_1\cap J=I$. On $D_+(x_i)$ divide homogeneous numerators by powers of $x_i$. The ideal of $Y$ is $(\mathfrak p_1B[x_i^{-1}])_0/(IB[x_i^{-1}])_0$, and its $Q$th power is the corresponding image of $\mathfrak p_1^Q$: multiplying numerators proves one inclusion, and decomposing a homogeneous element of an ideal power into homogeneous products proves the other, inserting powers of $x_i$ to make each fraction degree zero. Finite intersections commute with this localization: for membership in both ideals multiply the two witnessing denominators. Thus the kernel of restriction of $\mathcal I_Y^Q$ to $\mathcal O_C$ is zero on every chart, and hence zero as a sheaf. The quotient charts and the ideal-power convention used here are [def-pc-proj, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers].

proof.text: For $t\ge Q$ the inclusion $\mathcal I_Y^t\subseteq\mathcal I_Y^Q$ follows from the definition of ideal powers. Consequently restriction of $\mathcal I_Y^t$ is still injective. Trivialize $L^{\otimes m}$ on each projective chart using [def-pc-projective-space-twist]; tensoring the injection there is the identity operation on a free rank-one factor, and the resulting injections glue. A global section in the restriction kernel is therefore zero on every chart and is zero by the sheaf axiom. This gives precisely the asserted injection into $H^0(C,L^{\otimes m}|_C)$ for every $m\ge0$.

proof.text: Set $\mathfrak p_a=\sqrt{Q_a}$. Prime membership gives $V_+(J)=\bigcup_{a\ne1}V_+(\mathfrak p_a)$: a prime containing a finite intersection contains one factor (take a product of counterexamples otherwise). Thus $|X|=Y\cup|C|$. The generic point of $Y$ is absent from $C$, since minimality of $\mathfrak p_1$ and distinct radicals imply no $\mathfrak p_a\subseteq\mathfrak p_1$ for $a\ne1$. Every other dimension-one component remains in $C$. Every embedded primary support has dimension zero, since it is a proper irreducible closed subset of a component of a dimension-one scheme, so no new dimension-one component appears. At the generic prime of any remaining component, the removed factor becomes the unit ideal by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-primary-decomposition]; hence $I$ and $J$ have identical localized ideals there, and the degree-zero chart local rings of $X$ and $C$ coincide. Their lengths, and therefore their generic multiplicities, are equal.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components] to $X$ and $L$, and then to $C$ and $L|_C$. Both are proper of dimension at most one; their twists are invertible by [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. This gives finite positive generic lengths, in particular $\mu\ge1$, and
$$\deg(L)=\mu\deg(L|_Y)+\deg(L|_C).$$
The equality uses exactly the remaining components and identical generic local rings of Step 4, and includes the empty sum. By [lem-sc-normalization-exists], $\widetilde Y$ is integral proper of dimension one and $\nu$ is birational. Apply [lem-per-birational-curve-degree-invariance] to obtain $\deg(L|_Y)=\deg(\nu^*L|_Y)=e$. Thus $\deg(L|_C)=\deg(L)-\mu e$.

source.place: Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components); Tag 0AYU (lemma-degree-birational-pullback); normalization finiteness as in lem-sc-normalization-exists.

proof.text: The degree-one case of [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-dimension] gives $dm+c=\chi(X,L^{\otimes m})$ at all integers. By [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], $\deg(L)=P_X(1)-P_X(0)=d$. For $C\ne\varnothing$, apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] and [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_C$ and the single invertible module $L|_C$. This gives a polynomial $R$ of degree at most one with $R(m)=\chi(C,L^{\otimes m}|_C)$ at all integers. Its slope is $R(1)-R(0)=\deg(L|_C)=d-\mu e$ and $c_C=R(0)\in\mathbf Z$. To identify it with the specified coordinate polynomial, use [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal] on $C$ and [lem-sfb-projective-coordinate-ring-euler-polynomial] on its canonical ideal. Their eventual equality says exactly that $R$ is the coordinate Hilbert polynomial. Since coordinate dimensions are nonnegative for arbitrarily large $m$, its slope is nonnegative. If $C=\varnothing$, sections and Euler characteristics vanish by [lem-sfb-projective-twist-euler-section-uniqueness], so $P_C=0$, $c_C=0$ and $\deg(L|_C)=0$, giving the same formula.

source.place: Tag 0BEM (lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler), Tag 0AYR (definition-degree-invertible-sheaf), Tag 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0); Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module). Slopes identified by evaluating a linear polynomial at 1 and 0.

proof.text: For the final assertion apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to see that $X$ is Noetherian. The finite-component assertion of [lem-sc-component-intersections-finite] then applies. A dimension-zero component would be a closed singleton disjoint from all the others, hence also open; connectedness and dimension one rule this out. If $Y\ne|X|$, let $Z$ be the nonempty union of all other components, all of dimension one. If $Y\cap Z$ were empty these two closed sets would partition $X$ into nonempty clopen sets, contradicting [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Choose $P\in Y\cap Z$. Its membership in an intersection of distinct components makes it closed by [lem-sc-component-intersections-finite]. Step 4 places $Z$ inside $C$, so $P\in Y\cap C$ lies on a dimension-one component of $C$.

The item statement differs from base only in the clarified codomain of the restriction map, H^0(C,L^m|_C), plus stmt_deps for module pullback and sheaf tensor product; nothing is weakened. New node lem-sfb-homogeneous-primary-decomposition: graded Lasker (Altman-Kleiman 20.27) with radical-power and localization clauses. It is true, and I checked it on (x^2), (xy) and (x^2,xy). It is not a duplicate: lem-per-noetherian-primary-decomposition gives ordinary primary factors only, and the krull/normal-dichotomy and p-primary torsion nodes are unrelated. It does not restate a clause of the item. Steps: (1) p_1 is minimal, because any minimal prime below it is homogeneous by the new node and a smaller homogeneous prime is still relevant; C=Proj(B/J) is proper and lies in X. (2) On each chart the kernel is ((p_1^Q cap J)B_xi)_0, which lies in (I B_xi)_0. (3) Tensoring with invertible L^m keeps the injection. (4) Supports and identical generic local rings, via the unit-ideal localization. (5) 0AYW degree sum, normalization, then 0AYU birational invariance. (6) The coordinate polynomial of C equals the Euler polynomial via Snapper and the canonical-ideal Euler node; delta>=0; the empty case is covered. (7) Connectedness rules out 0-dimensional components and gives a closed point P in Y cap C. Examples checked: double line (C empty, delta=0); two lines (P_C=m+1); embedded point (delta=0). Advisory: the 'precisely' clause in step 4 relies on step 7's exclusion of 0-dimensional components.
